name: Brake Cooling
description: Ducts that take high-pressure air from the front fascia/splitter and feed it to the eye (center) of each front rotor so the vanes pump it out through the ring. A heavy (~3,700 lb) car with 600+ hp needs ducting to keep pads in their window and fluid below boiling. Rear ducting is optional.

components.name: Brake duct inlets (fascia / splitter)
components.description: Inlet openings in the high-pressure zone of the front fascia or splitter with a round hose flange. Use existing fascia openings (fog-light/brake-duct apertures) where possible to avoid adding drag.
components.location: Lower front fascia, outboard, x≈-0.94, y≈0.30, z≈±0.55.

factory.name: ZL1/1LE fascia openings and underbody air guides (exact GM brake-cooling parts not confirmed in sources)

raceOptions.name: Fabricated / carbon 3 in (76 mm) inlet flange or NACA in splitter
raceOptions.notes: 3 in is common; 3.5–4 in for endurance.

hardware.item: Inlet flange rivets / M5 screws to fascia/splitter

installNotes: Fit after fascia/splitter is final (phase 10), but plan hose path in phase 4.
inspection: Clear debris/grass from inlets after off-track moments.

modelRef.dimensions: Oval ~160 x 120 mm face to 3 in (76 mm) spigot
modelRef.features: Carbon bell-mouth with flange behind the fascia brake opening

components.name: Brake duct hose
components.description: High-temperature flexible duct (silicone/Kevlar or SCAT-type) from inlet to backing plate, with enough slack for steering lock and suspension travel.
components.location: Front wheel well / behind fascia, along the inner fender to the knuckle.

raceOptions.name: 3 in high-temp brake duct hose (silicone-coated fiberglass/Kevlar)

hardware.item: Hose clamps / safety-wire wraps each end
hardware.spec: 3 in worm clamp or 0.032 in safety wire

installNotes: Turn lock-to-lock at full bump/droop: hose must not kink, touch the tire, or pull off.
inspection: Check for melted/chafed hose every event.

modelRef.dimensions: 3 in (76 mm) ID, ~1.0 m per side
modelRef.features: Red corrugated high-temp hose with wire helix, clamped at both ends

components.name: Brake duct backing plates (rotor-eye ducts)
components.description: Plate that replaces the factory dust shield, bolting to the knuckle and directing duct air into the rotor eye/hat center (not onto the rotor face).
components.location: Front knuckle behind the rotor, duct outlet at the hat center, z≈±0.62.

raceOptions.name: Fabricated aluminum backing plate with 3 in spigot (Gen 6 specific kits exist)

installNotes: Install in place of the dust shield before the hub/rotor; check clearance to rotor (≥ 5 mm) at full steering lock.
inspection: Check plate for cracks and rotor rub marks.

sources.title: TightTorque – Chevrolet Camaro 6 (2016–2024) torque table, compiled from GM 2016–2018 Camaro service manual sections

modelRef.dimensions: Plate ~260 mm, 3 in spigot feeding the rotor eye
modelRef.features: Aluminium plate on the knuckle bolts with turned lip and hose spigot

components.name: Rear brake ducts (optional)
components.description: Underfloor NACA or scoop feeding 2–2.5 in hose to the rear rotor eye. Usually only needed for endurance or very heavy braking tracks.
components.location: Underfloor ahead of rear wheels to rear knuckles.
installNotes: Route clear of halfshafts and exhaust.

modelRef.features: Corrugated duct hose to the rear rotor eye

components.name: Rotor/caliper temperature paint & sensors
components.description: Thermal paint stripes on rotor edges and calipers (or IR rotor sensors logged to the dash) to verify ducting: target race-pad windows ~400–650 °C rotor, caliper body < ~200 °C, fluid well under its wet boiling point.
components.location: Rotor outer edge and caliper body; IR sensors on a bracket aimed at the rotor face.

raceOptions.name: Tempilaq / AP thermal paint; IR brake temperature sensors

installNotes: Apply three paint grades per rotor before shakedown.
inspection: Read paint after each session; repaint when all grades have changed.

modelRef.dimensions: M12 IR sensor ~40 mm, 25 mm from the rotor inboard face
modelRef.features: Stainless IR sensor on a bracket aimed at the friction face
